assertion.name: Subclinical Optic Neuropathy
assertion.description: Bilateral subclinical optic neuropathy detected only by optical coherence tomography was found in two unrelated BRPF1 patients. Because it is asymptomatic it is easily missed on routine examination; the finding is the basis for recommending OCT-inclusive ophthalmological evaluation. Evidence rests on two cases.
assertion.notes: Frequency deliberately omitted. The only source is a two-patient OCT series with no cohort denominator, and because detection requires OCT the observed rate in any cohort not systematically imaged is uninformative. Colson et al. 2025 note only that two patients with frameshift variants have been described with optic neuropathy.

selected_evidence.snippet: To date, only a few patients with BRPF1 variants have been described, and none were reported to have optic neuropathy.

assertion.name: Speech and Language Disorder
assertion.description: Speech and language difficulties are prominent but variably recorded. assertion.name: Reduced Motor Nerve Conduction Velocity
assertion.description: Markedly slowed motor conduction was reported in the original CNTNAP1 families, including velocities below 10 m/s. A later CNTNAP1 child had a distal median velocity of 11.1 m/s at three weeks. GLDN-associated conduction abnormalities can change with age; this is an electrophysiological readout, not a universal threshold distinguishing all subtypes.

reports_on.interpretation: Measured velocity reports peripheral conduction impairment. The original CNTNAP1 values below 10 m/s are cohort-specific and do not establish a diagnostic cutoff for the entire LCCS group.

selected_evidence.snippet: Nerve conduction velocity studies performed at 1 week of age demonstrated axonal motor and sensory neuropathy but were normal when repeated at 7 months of age.

value.name: Absent Fetal Movement
value.description: Reduced or absent prenatal movement across the LCCS spectrum. Total immobility at every ultrasound examination from 12 weeks or later characterized all 39 clinically defined Finnish LCCS cases; the frequency band refers to that series, not all genotypes or all gestational examinations. Reduced movement is a shared functional consequence of distinct motor-unit disorders and can also accompany NEK9 skeletal dysplasia. It can cause a fetal deformation sequence without explaining every primary skeletal, cerebral, vascular or visceral manifestation.
value.notes: This clinical state was previously annotated at organism scale in a duplicate pathophysiology entry.

assertion.description: Reduced prenatal movement can produce joint webbing within the arthrogryposis deformation sequence. The exact timing and why webbing occurs in some subtypes but not others remain uncertain.

selected_evidence.snippet: Non-syndromic or isolated AMC arises as a result of reduced or absent fetal movements, which can result in a range of defects, including pterygia, pulmonary hypoplasia, and craniofacial defects.

assertion.name: Neonatal Respiratory Failure
assertion.description: Respiratory failure at or soon after birth is documented in multiple LCCS subtypes. The original PIP5K1C kindred had five liveborn affected infants, all dying of respiratory insufficiency within minutes to hours; this is not an umbrella mortality estimate. GLDN cases demonstrate variable contributions from pulmonary hypoplasia, diaphragm paralysis and airway abnormalities, with central apnea separately documented in one child. Absent respiratory drive is not established across all subtypes, and some survivors later wean from ventilation.
assertion.notes: This clinical state was previously annotated at organism scale in a duplicate pathophysiology entry.

selected_evidence.snippet: He required extensive resuscitation at birth including intubation, ventilation, chest compressions, and epinephrine administration, developed progressive respiratory failure, pneumothoraces, and pulmonary hemorrhage, and died at 40 hours of age

assertion.name: Hypercalcemia
assertion.description: Elevated serum calcium driven by extrarenal 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D synthesis by granuloma macrophages, with optional PTHrP secretion. Affects approximately 5-10% of patients and may cause nephrolithiasis or nephrocalcinosis.

selected_evidence.snippet: Hypercalcemia in sarcoidosis is due to three mechanistic reasons: (1) systemic conversion of 25-hydroxyvitamin D to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D by the enzyme 1-alpha hydroxylase produced by activated monocyte/macrophage system, (2) production of parathormone-related peptide (PTHrP) by the sarcoid granuloma, (3) tissue-level conversion of 25-hydroxyvitamin D to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D by 1-alphahydroxylase produced by local monocyte/macrophage system in the sarcoid granuloma.

assertion.name: Uveitis
assertion.description: Eye inflammation that can lead to vision impairment if untreated. May be anterior, posterior, or panuveitis.

selected_evidence.snippet: Uveitis was the most common ocular manifestation.

value.name: Cardiac Sarcoidosis
value.description: Myocardial granulomas causing conduction abnormalities, heart failure, or sudden death.

assertion.name: Atrioventricular Block
assertion.description: Conduction system involvement from myocardial granulomas. AV block (often high-grade) is a common cardiac sarcoidosis presentation; QRS prolongation greater than 120 ms is a screening indicator.

selected_evidence.snippet: male gender, a QRS duration > 120 ms, and nsVT on Holter monitoring were identified as significant markers associated with the presence of cardiac sarcoidosis

assertion.name: Mediastinal Lymphadenopathy
assertion.description: Symmetric enlargement of hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes, often the presenting finding on chest radiograph.

selected_evidence.snippet: Although intrathoracic involvement is the hallmark of the disease, present in over 90% of patients, sarcoidosis can affect virtually any organ.
